---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "Alphabetical reference of TimeToAlign! model terminology"
---

This page collects all terms introduced in the [Conceptual Model](concepts.qmd).
Hover over any {{< glossary glossary >}}-highlighted term elsewhere on this site
to see its definition.

For the full context in which each term is introduced, follow the cross-references
to the relevant section of the conceptual model.


## A

**Accolade**
:   One line of a page of music (a system), read from left to right: one
    horizontal piece of the page's {{< glossary "Time path" >}}, and the
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} along it. An accolade is as long as its piece,
    states the area of the image it stands for in `meta["box"]` and the
    image in `meta["image"]`, and holds the {{< glossary Box >}}es of the
    areas lying on it. A page is the {{< glossary SegmentLine >}} of its
    accolades, a volume the segment line of its pages; neither states an
    area. `TimeAxisPath.from_boxes()` finds the accolades among the areas
    of a page given in reading order: a box begins a new accolade when its
    left edge lies left of the previous box's by more than half the span of
    all left edges (`group_into_accolades`).
    See [How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes](howto/how01_graphical_boxes.ipynb).

**AlignmentAnchor**
:   A coordinate pair associating one coordinate on timeline A with one on
    timeline B; a neutral record with no claim semantics---provenance is
    carried by the enclosing {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}. Only synchronous
    MatchClaims produce AlignmentAnchors. From a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}
    of {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}}s, one derives a **StartAnchor** and
    an **EndAnchor**.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**AlignmentBundle**
:   A collection of {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}s with inter-group
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} connections; provides coordinate transfer via
    offset arithmetic, interpolation, and {{< glossary WarpMap >}}s.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**AlignmentMatrix**
:   An audio-to-audio alignment in which several recordings of one work are each
    warped onto a single shared, equidistant reference grid. Per recording, a
    parallel onset-time array gives that recording's clock-time at each grid
    column; because every array indexes the same grid they are equal length, so
    together they form a dense matrix of shape (recordings × grid columns). A
    single such file encodes an entire {{< glossary MatchGraph >}} directly ---
    every pair of recordings is related at every grid column --- rather than
    only one score-to-performance correspondence. The complete pairwise claim
    set is held in a {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**Atomic section**
:   A stretch of a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s axis that its flow control
    never divides: an interval between consecutive coordinates of its
    {{< glossary Jump >}}s, {{< glossary JumpTarget >}}s,
    {{< glossary Break >}}s and {{< glossary SectionBreak >}}s and the places
    their {{< glossary Destination >}}s go on at, named by a letter (`A`, `B`,
    ..., `Z`, `AA`, ...) in the order of the axis. Every flow is a sequence of
    atomic sections. `Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control()` writes
    them as {{< glossary Region >}}s stating the type `tts:AtomicSection`, and
    the computed {{< glossary FlowMap >}}s list them.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

## B

**BeatGrid**
:   An ordered set of **BeatGridSegment**s and the beats they generate on a
    seconds axis. Each segment states one stretch of a recording --- an anchor
    instant, a tempo, a {{< glossary BeatPolicy >}}, and which beat of a bar
    the anchor is --- and generates beats without end; the grid orders the
    segments, bounds each by its successor's start and the last by its extent,
    and labels the resulting beats with measure and beat numbers. Each labelled
    beat is a **GridBeat**. A BeatGrid is *not* a
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} and stores nothing per beat.
    See [How to Build Beat Grids](howto/how01_beat_grids.ipynb).

**BeatPolicy**
:   How one bar is counted in beats: a grouping cycle over one counted note
    value. A 4/4 bar is four beats of a quarter, a compound 6/8 bar two beats
    of three eighths, an uneven (3+2+3)/8 bar three beats of unequal length.
    Beat lengths are derived from the grouping and the division, never stored.
    One signature admits more than one counting: a {{< glossary BeatGrid >}}'s
    lattice reads 6/8 as six beats of an eighth, because its beat-in-bar index
    counts the notated value rather than the felt pulse.

**BoundingBox**
:   An axis-aligned area of an image: `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` (the
    `xywh` of IIIF and Media Fragments), in image space (origin the image's
    top-left corner, x right, y down), all four in one unit and one number
    type; `width` and `height` are never negative. A shape, as is
    {{< glossary Quadrilateral >}}: built with `from_xywh()`,
    `from_corners()` (MEI's `ulx`, `uly`, `lrx`, `lry`) or
    `from_media_fragment()`, and written with `to_dict()`,
    `as_media_fragment()`, `as_svg_points()` and `as_mei_zone()`. Its
    numbers are never rounded: a value the axis cannot hold exactly (385.5
    on `pixels`) is refused. Every shape has a bounding box, the smallest
    BoundingBox holding it.
    See [How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes](howto/how01_graphical_boxes.ipynb).

**Box**
:   An area of an image as an interval event of a graphical
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} running along a horizontal piece of the
    image's {{< glossary "Time path" >}}, such as an
    {{< glossary Accolade >}} of a page. A Box holds
    exactly one shape, a {{< glossary BoundingBox >}} or a
    {{< glossary Quadrilateral >}}, in the image's space, and the interval
    of the shape's x extent on its timeline: `start` is the shape's `x_min`
    less the x at which the timeline stands in its image (the x of its
    `meta["box"]`, 0 where it states none), `duration` is
    `x_max − x_min`. `Box.from_shape(shape, origin=, id=)` makes it; adding
    a Box whose interval contradicts its shape, or whose shape is on another
    unit or number type than the timeline, is refused on every path that
    adds events, a package read included. `DmosLoader` and
    `MeiFacsimileLoader` read Boxes onto the accolades of their pages and
    name them with `box_ids`; an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}}'s
    `to_file()` writes every timeline's Boxes beside the manifest in one
    table, `boxes.parquet`, named in its `resources` with the type `Box`
    (see {{< glossary Resource >}}), and `from_file()` reads them back.
    See [How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes](howto/how01_graphical_boxes.ipynb).

**Barline**
:   A {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}} recording a barline the source
    prints (a double or a final barline). It changes nothing in the flow.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**Break**
:   A {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}} at which the flow does not go
    on: when the flow plays up to it, a {{< glossary Jump >}} at the same
    coordinate with a {{< glossary Destination >}} that holds is taken,
    otherwise the flow ends there and begins again at the next
    {{< glossary SectionBreak >}}, if any. With `ends` (a condition:
    `passes`, `after`) it ends the flow only while that condition holds, as a
    *Fine* does after a *D.C.* or *D.S.* A Break lies between two brackets of
    alternative endings.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

## C

**Catalogue**
:   Data shipped with the TimeToShare package that guides the writing of
    {{< glossary statement >}}s and that tools read to offer properties
    and values and to print pairs in words: the `prefixes` of the
    vocabularies its patterns use, from which a written manifest's inline
    `@context` takes those its statements use; `aliases`, namespaces read as
    equal (`https://schema.org/` as `http://schema.org/`); the identifier
    `systems` (Wikidata, MusicBrainz, the GND, VIAF, MeLODy with LRMoo,
    IMSLP and others, and the fallback vocabularies that state a relation
    where a system has no property of its own); the `verbs`, relations in
    words (`is_a`, `performed_by`, `part_of`, …) each with a pattern per
    system; and the `types` of thing a subject or value is. The validators
    never consult it. `add_verb()` states a verb in one system's vocabulary,
    and `get_rectangles()` gathers the pairs it reads as one verb about one
    thing.
    See [How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For](howto/how03_describe_the_work.ipynb) and
    [TimeToShare's description of a manifest](https://github.com/TimeToAlign/TimeToShare/blob/main/docs/description.md), section 10.

**ChainMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} that applies multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s in sequence, creating a conversion
    path from a source unit to a target unit.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Child**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} nested within a parent, sharing its
    measuring unit but defining its own origin. `add_child()` locks a child
    by default, which prevents side effects from modifications. An unlocked
    child's length may change only within its parent's known length: a
    parent never grows because a child grew. A child holds its parent's
    positions from its start up to its end, and its end only where no
    sibling starts there; a nested timeline is reached only through
    parents that all hold the position. A child created with
    `measures=True` holds the slice of its parent's measure map over its
    span; by default it holds none.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**ClaimType**
:   The semantic kind of a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}, derived from its
    structure rather than stored --- read from whether the claim is
    synchronous and whether both of its sides name an event or one names
    the {{< glossary NOMATCH >}} sentinel. Every MatchClaim names an event
    on each side it aligns; a side without an event of its own is given a
    {{< glossary Projection >}} first. Three members: **event_match**
    (synchronous, an event on each side; the case that yields
    {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s), **nomatch** (non-synchronous, one
    event and the sentinel on the other side; see {{< glossary NOMATCH >}}),
    and **conceptual** (non-synchronous, an event on each side --- a
    structural correspondence with no temporal commitment). What a
    {{< glossary MatchGraph >}} infers through groups is the graph's own
    inferred edge and has no kind here.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**CombinationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} yielding outputs from multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s simultaneously (e.g., *(x, y)*
    coordinate pairs).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Commensurability**
:   Two timelines are commensurable if connected by a chain of
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s, membership in the same
    {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}, or cross-group
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s, enabling coordinate translation between them.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**Commensurable**
:   See {{< glossary Commensurability >}}.

**Complete form**
:   The form in which `to_dict(minimal=False)` writes a
    {{< glossary "TimeToShare manifest" >}}: every key the format
    defines is written, those holding their default value included (`null`,
    `{}`, `[]`). A key whose default is its absence, such as a manifest's `id`
    or a root timeline's `offset`, is written only when it has a value. The
    complete and the {{< glossary "Minimal form" >}} of one object read back to
    equal objects, and each writes back to itself.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

**ConcatenationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} combining bounded
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s such that each coordinate region is
    handled by a specific map.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Contiguity**
:   A {{< glossary TimeInterval >}} is contiguous if it monotonically
    spans all coordinates between its start and end. An
    {{< glossary Instant >}} is contiguous with a TimeInterval if it is
    synchronous with its {{< glossary EndInstant >}}.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**ConversionMap**
:   A typed function attached to a {{< glossary Timeline >}} that maps each
    coordinate to exactly one value (coordinate, label, or filename); also
    permits inverse conversion back to the timeline's own unit. Also called
    **C-map**.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Coordinate**
:   A position on a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, expressed as the distance
    from the origin in the timeline's measuring unit. Combines a numeric
    value with a TimeUnit. The unit alone decides the number policy:
    `quarters` and `beats` are exact `Fraction`s, discrete units (`ticks`,
    `samples`, `frames`, `pixels`) are locked to `int`, and the remaining
    continuous units (`seconds`, `points`, `centimeters`, …) are `float`.
    That declared number type is preserved at every boundary — authored,
    converted, offset-computed, interpolated, queried or retrieved — so a
    fraction-canonical axis always yields `Fraction`s and a float-canonical
    axis always yields `float`s. An explicit `number_type=` overrides the
    default, and exact input is never degraded.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## D

**Destination**
:   One place a {{< glossary Jump >}} may go on at, and when: a
    `JumpDestination`. Its place is `to` (the {{< glossary "element id" >}}
    of a {{< glossary JumpTarget >}}, a {{< glossary Region >}}, a child
    timeline or the timeline itself), `by` (a signed distance from the Jump;
    `by: 0` is going on and is never taken) or neither (the start of its
    section). Its conditions all must hold: `passes` (the arrivals at the
    Jump that count), `repeat_count` (taken at most that often), `after`
    (another Jump's destination must have been taken) and `determined`
    (false for a choice nobody can check, such as an ossia, which is never
    taken). `reset` says whether going back restores the Jumps and Breaks
    gone back over, as a repeat does; a *D.C.* or *D.S.* played without
    repeats states `reset: false`.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**DictStore**
:   A generic `EventStore` subclass holding a `dict[str, EventData]` with
    arbitrary keys. Used internally by AlignmentLoaders to store one
    `EventData` table per timeline-to-be (e.g., `"score:clt_1"`,
    `"perf:Chopin_op10_no3_p01:cpt_1"`).
    Maintains the uniform `EventStore` interface.
    See the [API reference](reference/DictStore.qmd).

**Discrete**
:   A timeline is discrete when coordinates exist only at discrete points
    (e.g., pixels, samples, ticks). Contrast with Continuous timelines
    where coordinates can take any real value (e.g., seconds, quarters).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Domain**
:   One of three temporal categories: **Graphical** (visual/spatial),
    **Logical** (symbolic/musical), or **Physical** (audio/sound). Each
    domain has both discrete and continuous timeline variants.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## E

**element id**
:   The id that identifies an element of a manifest: the manifest's own, a
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} (root or descendant),
    {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}, MeasureMap,
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} at any nesting depth,
    {{< glossary Region >}}, {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}},
    {{< glossary FlowMap >}}, {{< glossary "Virtual timeline" >}} or
    {{< glossary Resource >}}. It is unique across
    the whole manifest and every kind, so the id alone names the element. An
    id is free: whatever was given is kept verbatim, any non-empty string
    without a control character; spaces, colons, slashes and URIs are
    allowed, and no word is reserved. Only an element given no id gets a
    minted one, `{prefix}_{N}` with `N` above the highest number held under
    that prefix, so a number once given is never given again. The prefix
    names the kind: `clt`, `dlt`,
    `cpt`, `dpt`, `cgt` or `dgt` for a timeline (continuous or discrete,
    logical, physical or graphical), `group` for a group, `measuremap` for
    a MeasureMap, `cmap`, `lmap`, `tmap` or `pmap` for a conversion map,
    `region` for a Region, `resource` for a Resource, `jump`, `jump_target`,
    `break`, `section_break` or `barline` for a flow-control element and
    `flow_map` for a FlowMap; a virtual timeline is minted as a timeline of
    its unit; a loader role leads it (`score:clt_1`). When trees are joined into a group or bundle, a
    minted id that collides is re-minted and a given id that collides raises,
    for every kind of element. The id identifies, the `name` displays: a name
    may be absent or repeat, and an id is never derived from it.

**EndInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the end of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Its coordinate must be greater than or
    equal to the corresponding {{< glossary StartInstant >}}'s coordinate.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Event**
:   Anything associated with a {{< glossary Timeline >}} via
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s. An {{< glossary InstantEvent >}} has zero
    duration; a {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}} has duration defined by
    start and end coordinates.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## F

**Finding**
:   What playing flow control found, without raising: a flow that never ends
    (`endless_loop`), a flow ending at a {{< glossary Break >}} that states no
    condition before the end (`flow_ends_at_break`), two
    {{< glossary Destination >}}s of one Jump holding at once
    (`ambiguous_targets`), a destination nobody can check
    (`undetermined_target`), and a stretch never played (`never_played`).
    The `default` and `single` flows have findings, the `printed` flow none;
    `Timeline.get_flow(convention)` returns them with the flow. A finding
    may name its cause (`FlowFinding.cause`, a `FlowFindingCause`): a
    stretch the `single` flow leaves out that the `default` flow plays has
    the cause `single_playback` (going through once takes the last volta
    ending).
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**Flow control element**
:   One of the elements a {{< glossary Timeline >}} holds as its flow control
    (a manifest's `flow_control` array): a {{< glossary Jump >}}, a
    {{< glossary JumpTarget >}}, a {{< glossary Break >}}, a
    {{< glossary SectionBreak >}} or a {{< glossary Barline >}}. Each lies at
    one coordinate and has an {{< glossary "element id" >}}; how it looks in
    the source is its `manifestation`, which decides nothing. An element is
    never changed or deleted to repair flow control: an actor's belief
    `"false"` rejects it (`flow_control.with_belief()`), and the right one is
    added. `Timeline.get_flow()` plays the elements no actor rejects.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**FlowMap**
:   One order in which stretches of one root {{< glossary Timeline >}} are
    played: an ordered list of chunks, each the ID of a
    {{< glossary Region >}}, a child timeline or a
    {{< glossary "Virtual timeline" >}} of that timeline's tree, or a `Gap` in
    which nothing of the timeline is played. A FlowMap holds no interval;
    resolved against its timeline (`resolve()`) it places each stretch where
    the one before it ends and converts positions both ways: `unfold()` takes
    a position of the timeline to every position it is played at, `fold()` a
    position of the flow to the position it plays, or None in a gap.
    `Timeline.create_flow_map(chunks)` creates and attaches one;
    `Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control()` writes the flows of the
    flow control (`default`, `single`, `printed`) as FlowMaps over the
    {{< glossary "Atomic section" >}}s.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

## G

## I

**IdCoordinate**
:   A {{< glossary Coordinate >}} that also names the {{< glossary Timeline >}}
    it belongs to. It is the default return of every coordinate getter in the
    library — stamps, timelines, groups, bundles, match lines, graphs and warp
    maps all hand back `IdCoordinate(value, unit, timeline_id)` unless an
    explicit `format=` asks for something else. Carrying identity is what lets
    a retrieved coordinate be handed straight back as a query without restating
    which axis it came from. An IdCoordinate never compares equal to a plain
    Coordinate in either direction; use `format="coordinate"` when timeline
    identity should be discarded.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Instant**
:   Associates a {{< glossary Coordinate >}} (a "time-point") with a
    signification such as "start of event *e*". Instants sharing a
    coordinate are synchronous.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**InstantEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} defined by a single {{< glossary Instant >}},
    having zero duration.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Interval**
:   A frozen scalar pairing two plain {{< glossary Coordinate >}}s as a
    half-open span `[start, end)`: the start is inclusive, the end exclusive.
    Both endpoints must share one TimeUnit and one number type, which makes the
    interval's own `unit` and `number_type` unambiguous; its `duration` is
    exactly `end - start`, returned as a `Duration`. Reversed intervals raise;
    zero-length ones are valid. It renders through the same formatter the
    scalars use, so an interval on a `quarters` axis prints
    `[1/2, 3/2) quarters` rather than `[0.5, 1.5)`. Interval is the scalar leaf
    of interval retrieval: `TimeIntervalStamp.get_interval()` and
    `TimelineGroup.get_interval_for()` both return one.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**IntervalField**
:   The `SemanticField` paired with {{< glossary Interval >}}. It stores a
    struct of `start` and `end` coordinate structs under one `unit`, `domain`,
    and `number_type` metadata triple, materialises `Interval | None` per row,
    and exposes vectorized `start`, `end`, and `duration` accessors returning
    `CoordinateField`, `CoordinateField`, and `DurationField`.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**InverseMap**
:   The reverse transformation of a bijective
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## J

**Jump**
:   A {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}} where the flow may leave the
    axis, holding one {{< glossary Destination >}} for every place it may go
    on at: a repeat end, a *D.C.*, a *D.S.*, a *To Coda* and the brackets of
    alternative endings at one coordinate are destinations of one Jump. When
    the flow plays up to it, of the destinations that hold one is taken (one
    going back with `reset` first, then one going back without, then one
    ahead, the nearest first); when none holds, the flow goes on.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**JumpTarget**
:   A {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}} marking a place a
    {{< glossary Destination >}} names by its {{< glossary "element id" >}}:
    a repeat start, a segno, a coda, a bracket. Nothing happens when the
    flow plays up to it.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

## L

**Length**
:   The distance between a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s origin and its last
    {{< glossary Instant >}}, or `None` when it is not known (see
    {{< glossary "Unknown length" >}}).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Locked**
:   A timeline state that fixes its coordinate axis: no
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s may be added after the last time-point, so its
    length cannot change. Locking governs the coordinate axis only ---
    non-structural annotations such as {{< glossary Region >}}s may still be
    added to a locked timeline. A timeline is locked with `locked=True`, when
    `add_child()` embeds it as a {{< glossary Child >}} with its default
    `locked=True`, or after construction with `lock()`; a child read from a
    manifest keeps the manifest's `locked`. A lock cannot be lifted. A locked
    timeline's length may still be unknown. On a locked timeline, setting
    `length`, `append_child()` and `append_segment()` raise `RuntimeError`,
    and content, a child or a MatchClaim position
    (`AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims()`) past its end is refused with a
    `ValueError` before anything is added, unless `add_events()` or
    `add_child()` is given `allow_expansion=True`;
    `create_child_from_region()` gives a child of any region within its
    length. A loader locks a timeline whose source states its length:
    `AudioLoader` a recording at the file's length, a score loader a score
    whose measures all state their length, at the end of its last measure or
    of its last event, whichever is later. Containment does not depend on
    the lock: a child, locked or not, ends within its parent's known length,
    and content or a child added into an unlocked timeline grows that
    timeline only.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

## M

**Match**
:   See {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}.

**MatchfileLoader**
:   Loader for Vienna Match (`.match`) alignment files. Uses the standard
    two-step `load()` → `create_*()` pattern. A single instance processes
    all `.match` files that share the same score, building a shared score
    timeline on the first file and verifying subsequent files against it.
    Returns an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} directly via
    `create_bundle()`. Score goes into its own group; performances
    are standalone timelines; {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s connect score to
    performances.
    See the [API reference](reference/MatchfileLoader.qmd).

**MatchClaim**
:   A claim of equivalence between two events on different timelines, each
    coordinate on its own timeline's axis, with its
    {{< glossary Provenance >}} (how it was made and who believes it) and a
    certainty. A side without an event of its own is given a
    {{< glossary Projection >}}. May be synchronous (producing
    {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s) or not: conceptual (structural
    equivalence without temporal commitment) or {{< glossary NOMATCH >}}
    (an event on one side, the sentinel on the other). A MatchClaim is
    always stated: what a {{< glossary MatchGraph >}} infers through groups
    is the graph's own (its inferred edges), never a MatchClaim. A person
    stating claims is recorded as believing them `"true"`
    (`create_match_claims(..., actor=)`). A claim is never deleted: who
    disagrees records a belief `"false"` in it
    (`AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_belief()`), and every reader of
    claims, the MatchStamp and coordinate getters included, takes the
    belief filter (`believer=`, `beliefs=`; see
    {{< glossary Provenance >}}). Readers of claims take the same timeline
    filters: `timeline_ids` keeps a claim with any of the named timelines
    on either side, `within` a claim whose both timelines are in the set.
    Held individually, or in the bundle's one MatchClaim table, a
    {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}. Its ID never changes: a claim given
    none holds no ID until the {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} it joins
    mints `claim_N`, `N` above the highest held there; a MatchClaimField
    mints nothing. A MatchClaim is addressed by its ID alone: a bundle or
    field already holding an ID refuses a second claim under it, and
    merging bundles (`from_bundles()`) refuses, before anything is merged,
    two sources holding one ID.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchClaimField**
:   The MatchClaim table: a columnar, PyArrow-backed store holding a set of
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s of every kind as Arrow columns, one per
    property of a MatchClaim (the two timeline IDs, the start and end
    anchors, each holding `coordinate_a` and `coordinate_b` only, the row's
    timelines being theirs, `is_synchronous`, the `provenance` and
    `certainty`, the event IDs and names, and `id`), rather than as one
    frozen MatchClaim object per claim; its columns are TimeToShare's
    MatchClaim table. Each anchor coordinate is a cell naming its own `unit`
    and `number_type` beside its number. In memory (`table`) the number
    keeps both sides, `value` and the exact `numerator` / `denominator`; the
    **package form** (`package_table`, the table `to_parquet()` writes)
    writes it once, in the member its number type names (an int as
    `numerator` alone, a fraction as `numerator` and `denominator`, a float
    as `value` alone), the others null, and `from_package_table()` reads
    that form back, refusing a cell that does not stand as its number type
    says and a null coordinate. A fraction is read in any terms (`2/4` is
    the value `1/2`), and a claim gives an end on both sides or on neither.
    Either way a claim's coordinate comes back in its
    axis's declared number type instead of being flattened on the way
    through the column. Individual MatchClaims are materialised on demand when a row is
    indexed or iterated. Built vectorized via `from_columns()`, it is the
    scalable backing for dense {{< glossary AlignmentMatrix >}} alignments,
    where the complete pairwise topology of a whole work runs to roughly a
    million claims, and an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} keeps all its
    claims in one, `match_claim_table`. Shared provenance is held once at
    field level; only claims whose provenance differs carry it per row. The
    `table` property gives the field as an Arrow table, the shared provenance
    in its schema metadata under the key `timetoshare:provenance`, and
    `from_table()` reads it back unchanged; `to_parquet()` and
    `from_parquet()` write and read `match_claims.parquet` in the package
    form. An
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}}'s `to_file()` writes its table there,
    beside the manifest, named in the manifest's `resources` (see
    {{< glossary Resource >}}), and `from_file()` reads it back; writing over
    an existing table keeps every claim it holds (the succession rule: same
    timelines, events and anchors, only the provenance may differ).
    `to_dict()` renders the same table as `{"provenance": …, "rows": […]}`,
    one mapping per claim keyed by the columns, and `from_dict()` reads it
    back.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment) and
    [How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package](howto/how03_match_claims_package.ipynb).

**MatchGraph**
:   An auxiliary structure formed by extending {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s
    through shared coordinates; may be viewed as a hyperedge connecting
    multiple coordinates from different timelines. Connected components yield
    {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}s. Its edges are the anchors of the
    synchronous MatchClaims it was given (stated) and those
    `extend_to_groups()` infers through {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}
    membership (`inferred_edges`, each naming its group and the claim it
    comes from); an inferred edge is the graph's own, never a MatchClaim.
    `filter()` keeps the claims the unified filters choose (`timeline_id`
    and `timeline_ids` on either side, `within` both sides in the set, the
    belief filter, `stated_only` for no inferred edges) and rebuilds the
    graph from them, extended through the same groups. Each Match box
    M1--M15 in the Hendrix figure is a MatchGraph.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchLine**
:   An ordered sequence of {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s derived from
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s, sorted by coordinate on a source timeline;
    input for {{< glossary WarpMap >}} generation.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchPath**
:   A path traversal connecting matched events across multiple timelines
    (e.g., A -> B -> C), enabling indirect alignment.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchStamp**
:   The union of {{< glossary TimeStamp >}}s from groups synchronously
    connected by a {{< glossary MatchGraph >}}. Contains one coordinate per
    participating timeline. C-map conversion values are opt-in here: unlike
    {{< glossary TimeStamp >}}, where C-Maps are
    visible by default, `conversion_maps` on a MatchStamp getter
    (`bundle.get_matchstamp_at()`, `get_matchstamps_at()`, `get_matchstamp_table()`,
    `MatchClaim.get_matchstamp()`) defaults to `False` — across a large bundle
    they would bury the alignment answer.
    This is a per-context *default value* for a shared parameter, not a
    structural difference: MatchStamp implements the same `Stamp` interface
    as every other stamp type — `get_coordinate_for(timeline_id)` returns an
    {{< glossary IdCoordinate >}} by default and a plain number under
    `format="float"/"int"/"fraction"`, `get_unit()` converts through a C-map,
    `get_conversion_for()` reads label and structured map values,
    `present_timelines` lists available timelines, and `is_interpolated`
    identifies interpolation fallback. A stamp from any source keeps the
    identical structure, methods, and behaviour the `Stamp` contract
    guarantees; only the caller-visible default for one keyword argument
    varies by producing context. `within=` on a MatchStamp getter (and on
    `MatchStamp.filter_by_timelines()`) always keeps the queried timeline
    and selects among the others; on `get_matchstamp_table()` and a group's
    `get_timestamp_table()` it selects the table's columns; the MatchClaims the stamp is read from are
    chosen by the belief filter (`believer=`, `beliefs=`), and a stamp
    counts apart the timeline pairs a MatchClaim's anchor links and those
    an inferred edge links (`n_stated_pairs`, `n_inferred_pairs`).
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MeasureConstituent**
:   A measure of a measure map that is only part of its nominal measure: an
    anacrusis, or one constituent of a split measure. It carries
    `offset_within_measure`, the strictly positive quarter-note position at
    which it begins inside the nominal measure, and is the only measure class
    that does. A measure is classified as a constituent exactly when that
    offset is stated and non-zero: a shared measure number never marks a split
    measure, because alternative endings ("16a", "16b") share one too. A
    measure table states the offset in its `mc_offset` column; a Measure Map
    `.mm.json` file states none, so `MeasureMapLoader` applies the standard's
    one convention, a first row numbered 0 that is shorter than nominal being
    an anacrusis at offset nominal minus actual length. In a compressed
    measure-map row the offset is the `offset_within_measure` extension,
    written only when non-zero.

**MetricMap**
:   A table-based {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} from a quarter position to its
    measure count, built from explicit measure-boundary anchors rather than a
    uniform measure length. Correctly handles anacrusis (an incomplete first
    measure), irregular measures, varying time signatures, and repeat
    structure. Built directly from a Verovio timemap via
    `MetricMap.from_verovio_timemap()`. Not invertible — many quarters map to
    the same measure.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**MetricalPositionMap**
:   A {{< glossary CombinationMap >}} pairing a {{< glossary MetricMap >}} with
    a beat-in-measure map to return a metrical position `{mc, beat}` from a
    quarter coordinate. Adds a reverse lookup `quarters_at(mc, beat)` (metrical
    position to quarters) and `mn_at(quarters)` (quarters to measure-number
    label). A TimeToShare manifest writes it as a `MeasureBeatMap` over the
    measure map its meter map describes, each measure's count standing as its
    number; reading the manifest returns that `MeasureBeatMap`.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Minimal form**
:   The form in which every `to_dict()` writes a
    {{< glossary "TimeToShare manifest" >}} by default (`to_dict(minimal=False)`
    writes the {{< glossary "Complete form" >}}): every key holding its default
    value is left out, except a timeline's `length`, which both forms write.
    Readers supply every default left out, so a minimal manifest can be written
    by hand; the smallest names the version and one timeline with its `id`,
    `unit` and `length`. `to_file()` writes a manifest file in the form it was
    read in, and in the minimal form and canonical YAML for an object not read
    from a file.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

**MpmLoader**
:   Loader for an MPM-Toolbox project: a sibling `.msm` score, `.mpm` modelled
    performance, and `.mpr` project file (carrying an observed audio-to-score
    alignment) for one work. Uses the standard two-step `load()` →
    `create_*()` pattern. Builds a shared logical `"score"` group holding the
    notes in two units — a ticks {{< glossary Timeline >}} (also carrying every
    MPM markup event: `Tempo`, `Dynamics`, `Articulation`, …) and a quarters
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} — with a `TicksToQuarters` map and a modelled
    quarters→seconds `TableMap` integrated from the performance's tempo markup;
    and a physical `"perf"` group of observed onsets in seconds and samples.
    Emits one synchronous cross-group {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per score note
    (the MSM `xml:id` ↔ MPR `ref` join is a bijection). Reads the modelled
    performance and the observed alignment; never runs an aligner. Returns an
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.

**MultiMap**
:   An umbrella term for composed {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s:
    {{< glossary ChainMap >}} (sequential),
    {{< glossary CombinationMap >}} (parallel outputs), and
    {{< glossary ConcatenationMap >}} (regional).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## N

**NOMATCH**
:   A sentinel value in a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} explicitly encoding the
    absence of a corresponding event on the other timeline. The MatchClaim
    records both timeline IDs and names the event of the timeline that has
    it, but has no {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s; `is_synchronous` is
    always `False`.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

## O

**Origin**
:   The zero coordinate of a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, from which all
    positions are measured.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## P

**Parent**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} that contains one or more
    {{< glossary Child >}} timelines. The parent and all its children must
    share the same measuring unit.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**PerformancePrecisionLoader**
:   Loader for audio-to-score alignment specimens: a directory bundling a
    `.solo` score, a Verovio timemap, and per-performer alignment files at the
    note, bar, and beat granularities. Uses the standard two-step `load()` →
    `create_*()` pattern. Resolves every `"<measure>+<offset>"` label to
    absolute quarters via a {{< glossary MetricMap >}}, builds one logical score
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} (quarters) and one physical performance
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} per recording (seconds), and emits a
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per alignment row — synchronous for located
    onsets, {{< glossary NOMATCH >}} for the dangling ones. Returns an
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.
    See the [API reference](reference/PerformancePrecisionLoader.qmd).

**ParangonadaLoader**
:   Loader for a *parangonar* *parangonada* export: per-performance CSV triples
    (score notes, performed notes, note-level correspondences) for one work.
    Uses the standard two-step `load()` → `create_*()` pattern. Parses the
    shared score once into two logical {{< glossary Timeline >}}s (quarters and
    division-grid ticks, linked by a divs→quarters `LinearMap`), builds one
    performance group per recording with two physical {{< glossary Timeline >}}s
    (seconds and samples, linked by a `SamplesToSeconds` map), and emits one
    cross-group {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per correspondence — synchronous for
    a matched note, {{< glossary NOMATCH >}} for a score-only or
    performance-only note. Reads the existing alignment; never runs an aligner.
    Returns an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.

**Projection**
:   An event standing on a timeline for an event that timeline does not
    hold, so that a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} can join two events: its ID
    (`projection_N` when none is given), its position on the timeline's own
    axis (`start`, and a `duration` for a span), and `projection_of`, the
    event it stands for (`{timeline_id, event_id}`), or none when its side
    was stated as a position only. `Timeline.add_projections()` adds
    Projections, reusing one the timeline already holds for the same event
    and position; `AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims()`, the alignment
    loaders and `match_notes_by_attributes()` give a Projection to every
    side stated as a position. A package holds every timeline's Projections
    in one table, the Projections table (`projections.parquet`, one row per
    Projection with its `timeline_id`), which an AlignmentBundle's
    `to_file()` writes beside the manifest whenever one of its timelines
    holds Projections, named in its `resources`, sorted by timeline ID, and
    `from_file()` reads back onto the timelines. In memory a Projection's
    `start` and `duration` are coordinate cells, each naming its unit and
    number type; the table writes them in the package form: the timeline's
    `unit` and `number_type` once per row, each number once, in the member
    its number type names (see {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}). A
    Projection's ID is unique among all Projections of its manifest: a
    missing one is minted above every Projection ID the manifest holds, a
    given one another timeline's Projection already holds is refused, and
    an ID once given is never re-minted. Timelines given Projections apart
    and joined later may hold one ID twice; writing their package refuses
    it, naming both timelines.
    See [Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims](tutorials/tut06_alignment_bundles.ipynb) and
    [How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package](howto/how03_match_claims_package.ipynb).

**Provenance**
:   How an item was made and who believes it, one facility for
    {{< glossary statement >}}s and {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s. Every key
    is optional, but an entry states at least one: who stated the item
    (`stated_by`), the day (`date`), how (`method`: `manual`, `reconciled`,
    `imported`, `inferred` or an IRI), the lookup `service`, the sources it
    rests on (`basis`), how closely a value matches (`match`), a `note`, and
    `beliefs`: at most one per actor, `"true"`, `"false"` or `"unlikely"`,
    with its date. A person stating an item is recorded as believing it
    `"true"`; a loader or a service records how it made the item and
    believes nothing. A belief never removes an item. The belief filter
    reads one actor's beliefs: `believer=` names the actor, and `beliefs=`
    the states kept, any of four: `"true"`, `"undecided"` (the believer
    holds no belief on the item), `"unlikely"` and `"false"`; the default
    keeps every state but `"false"`, and without a believer nothing is
    filtered. Actors compare as the IRIs they stand for under the
    manifest's `@context`, so one believer may be spelled twice in one
    entry; the entry is then read as the most critical of that believer's
    beliefs (`"false"` before `"unlikely"` before `"true"`). For a statement, the entry
    sits in the `provenance` beside an element's `statements` (or inside a
    value node, for its own pairs) and names the pair again by `property`
    and `value`; a subject has at most one entry per pair, and a pair
    without one is stated by the manifest's publisher. A pair held only as
    its entry is a candidate: `add_candidate()` offers one,
    `add_statement()` states it, `add_belief()` records a belief, and
    `get_candidates()` and `get_provenance()` take the belief filter. For a
    MatchClaim, the entry is the claim's `provenance`:
    `create_match_claims(..., actor=)` records the stating person's belief
    `"true"`, and `AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_belief()` records a belief in a claim
    the bundle holds.
    See [How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For](howto/how03_describe_the_work.ipynb),
    [Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims](tutorials/tut06_alignment_bundles.ipynb) and
    [TimeToShare's description of a manifest](https://github.com/TimeToAlign/TimeToShare/blob/main/docs/description.md), section 9.

## Q

**Quadrilateral**
:   An area of an image bounded by four corners, each a `Point` (`x`, `y`),
    held in the order `top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_right`,
    `bottom_left` (the order SVG polygons and IIIF selectors draw): it
    follows a measure of a scan whose sides are not upright. A shape, as is
    {{< glossary BoundingBox >}}. `from_points()` takes the corners in any
    order a source writes them, `order=` naming each one's role;
    `from_svg_points()` reads four SVG or MEI `points` starting at any
    corner and running either way. The corners held always run clockwise
    around a convex outline: `from_points()` refuses roles that do not, and
    points that bound no convex quadrilateral are refused, never reordered
    into one.
    See [How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes](howto/how01_graphical_boxes.ipynb).

## R

**raw_quarters**
:   The conventional name for the {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} (specifically
    a `ShiftMap`) attached to a score timeline. The timeline stores normalised
    (non-negative) coordinates — shifted so the minimum onset is `0.0` — and
    this map converts them back to the raw quarter values of the source. Its
    offset equals `min(raw_onsets)`. Added by {{< glossary MatchfileLoader >}}
    and `PartituraLoader` so downstream code can detect and apply the same
    shift when comparing coordinates across loaders.

**Reach**
:   The farthest coordinate on a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s own axis that its
    content reaches: the ends of its children (a {{< glossary Child >}} of
    {{< glossary "Unknown length" >}} contributing its offset plus its own
    reach), {{< glossary Region >}} ends, the coordinate of every
    {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}}, the place of every
    {{< glossary Destination >}} stating a distance (`by`), and the end of the
    measure map. Events are not part
    of it. A timeline without such content reaches 0. The reach is independent
    of the length; displays use it as the extent of a timeline of unknown
    length. Read it as `Timeline.reach`.

**Region**
:   A part of a {{< glossary Timeline >}} defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}, identified by its
    {{< glossary "element id" >}} and displayed by its `name` (e.g.,
    "Chorus", "Verse"). Regions are not timelines and cannot hold events or
    maps directly.
    See [Regions](concepts.qmd#regions).

**Resource**
:   An entry of a {{< glossary "TimeToShare manifest" >}}'s `resources`,
    naming a file that holds data for its timelines and lies beside it: its
    `id` (any {{< glossary "element id" >}} no other element of the manifest
    holds; an entry the library adds gets a minted `resource_N`, and an
    entry read keeps its own when written back), its `type` (what its rows are: `MatchClaim` for the
    MatchClaim table, a {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}, `Projection` for
    the Projections table, see {{< glossary Projection >}}, `Box` for the
    Box table, see {{< glossary Box >}}), the IDs of the
    `timelines` it holds data for, its `url` relative to the manifest, and
    optionally its `media_type`, `size` in bytes and `integrity` (an
    `Integrity`: `algorithm` and `digest`). At most one resource has each of
    the three types. A manifest and the files it names make a package; the
    manifest reads and draws without them, and names no event. An
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} keeps the entries as `Resource` objects
    in its `resources`; its `to_file()` writes the MatchClaim table when it
    holds MatchClaims, the Projections table when a timeline holds
    Projections and the Box table (`boxes.parquet`) when a timeline holds
    Boxes, each with its entry, and refuses to write event rows into
    the manifest beside them (`events=True`); `from_file()` reads them back.
    A named file that is absent is not read and its entry is kept.
    See the API reference ([Resource](reference/Resource.qmd),
    [Integrity](reference/Integrity.qmd)),
    [How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package](howto/how03_match_claims_package.ipynb) and
    [TimeToShare's README, "Resources and tables"](https://github.com/TimeToAlign/TimeToShare#resources-and-tables).

**Root**
:   The top-level {{< glossary Timeline >}} in a hierarchy of nested
    timelines. No parent bounds its length; an unlocked descendant grows
    only within its parent's known length, never pushing its parent.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**RotationMap**
:   A periodic {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} that wraps coordinates
    cyclically (e.g., an ostinato part that repeats while the main
    timeline advances).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## S

**ScoreNote**
:   A note or rest of a score: a `Note` written on a staff and in a voice.
    `staff` and `voice` are the source's numbers (an MEI `<staff>` and
    `<layer>`, a MuseScore staff and voice); a performance states neither, so
    a `Note` has no staff and no voice. Every other member, the pitch among
    them, is the `Note`'s. The score loaders write their notes as rows of
    event type `Note`; `get_field(ScoreNote)` on such rows reads them back as
    ScoreNotes where the table states an integer `staff` and `voice`, and
    `get_field(Note)` reads the same rows as Notes.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**SectionBreak**
:   A {{< glossary "Flow control element" >}} where a section ends (a
    movement, a section of a piece); the flow goes on across it. A
    {{< glossary Destination >}} without place goes on at the nearest
    SectionBreak before its {{< glossary Jump >}}, and a flow ended by a
    {{< glossary Break >}} begins again at the next one.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

**Segment**
:   A {{< glossary Child >}} timeline that is contiguous with its
    siblings. Segments enable concatenation of local coordinate systems.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**SegmentLine**
:   A runtime class parameterized by its segment class, such as
    `SegmentLine[DiscreteGraphicalTimeline]`, whose contiguous
    {{< glossary Segment >}}s tile its full length. A line is also an instance
    of that segment class. Any timeline can check the structure with the
    property `is_segment_line` and adopt enforcement with `as_segment_line()`; a line
    returns to an unenforced timeline with `to_timeline()`; both return a
    copy. Use `create_children_from_boundaries()` for boundary-driven tiling.
    Appending extends an unlocked line, while appending to a locked line
    raises `RuntimeError`. The segments of a line of known length keep
    ending at its length: a segment with a successor ends at the successor's
    offset, the last one at the line's end, and changing a segment's length
    never moves the line's end. A segment of unknown length ends at its
    successor's offset, or, the last one, at the line's known length.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**StartInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the start of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Statement**
:   A property–value pair saying what an element of a manifest stands for or
    how that thing relates to others. Three kinds of element carry
    `statements`: the manifest (the {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}}),
    which names the work it is about by `schema:about`; every
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} at any depth, for the manifestation it is
    the axis of; and every {{< glossary Region >}}, for the stretch it
    marks. A group carries none, and works and expressions are values, never
    elements. The property is `type` ("is a") or an IRI, compact
    (`prefix:suffix`, the prefix declared by the manifest's inline
    `@context`) or absolute; the value is a literal, a value object, a node
    (a thing, `{id: …}`, with its own pairs) or an ordered list. A value
    naming an element is its reference, `{id: "#cpt_1"}`; the library
    renames it with the element and drops the pair when the element leaves
    the manifest. Statements never nest, order or align timelines. A
    timeline and a bundle change them in place (`add_statement()`,
    `add_verb()`, `remove_statement()`), a frozen region returns a copy
    (`with_statement()`, `without_statement()`); each pair may carry a
    {{< glossary "provenance entry" >}}. `MeiHeadLoader` and
    `MelodyLoader` import them from an MEI header and from MeLODy's Turtle.
    See [How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For](howto/how03_describe_the_work.ipynb) and
    [TimeToShare's description of a manifest](https://github.com/TimeToAlign/TimeToShare/blob/main/docs/description.md).

**SupportPolicy**
:   How a cross-timeline {{< glossary MatchStamp >}} treats a timeline whose
    transferred coordinate falls outside *alignment support* --- the entering
    coordinate lies beyond the transferring {{< glossary WarpMap >}}'s anchor
    hull, or the produced coordinate would fall outside the target timeline's
    `[0, length]` span. `omit` (the default) drops that timeline; `clamp`
    reports the nearest in-support boundary coordinate; `extrapolate` keeps the
    linear extrapolation clipped to `[0, length]`. No policy ever yields a
    negative coordinate, and the queried timeline's own coordinate is never
    altered. Set per call on
    `AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_at(..., support_policy=...)` or persistently
    via `AlignmentBundle.support_policy`.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**Synchrony**
:   *Strict synchrony*: {{< glossary Instant >}}s sharing identical
    coordinates. *Pragmatic synchrony*: Instants binned together based on
    a threshold (e.g., for quantisation).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## T

**Time path**
:   The line a reader follows through an image (`TimeAxisPath`). No image
    has a time axis until its path is defined: a {{< glossary Timeline >}}
    of an image runs along the path and is as long as it. A path converts
    between its coordinate and the image's (x, y) with `to_2d()` and
    `from_2d()`. `HorizontalLinePath`, `VerticalLinePath`,
    `DiagonalLinePath` and `ParametricPath` are single lines; a
    `PiecewisePath` is made of consecutive pieces, such as the
    {{< glossary Accolade >}}s of a page, each starting where the ones
    before it end. `TimeAxisPath.from_boxes()` makes the path of a page
    from the areas drawn on it. `DmosLoader` and `MeiFacsimileLoader` make
    the paths of their pages (`create_paths()`); `IIIFManifestLoader` is
    given the path of each canvas.
    See [How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes](howto/how01_graphical_boxes.ipynb)
    and [How to Work with Graphical Timelines](howto/how01_graphical_timelines.ipynb).

**TimeInterval**
:   Defined by a {{< glossary StartInstant >}} and
    {{< glossary EndInstant >}}; left-inclusive and right-exclusive
    [*s*, *e*). The EndInstant's coordinate must be >= the StartInstant's.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} with duration, defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Contrast with
    {{< glossary InstantEvent >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalStamp**
:   Combination of a start {{< glossary TimeStamp >}} and an end
    TimeStamp, representing a cross-section of an interval through the
    timeline hierarchy. It stores one {{< glossary Interval >}} per timeline
    ID; `get_interval(timeline_id)` returns that Interval, `get_intervals()`
    the whole mapping, `get_duration_for()` an `IdDuration`, and
    `get_interval_in(unit)` the span converted through a C-map. Interval
    retrieval takes no `format` argument — its scalar leaf is always an
    Interval.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**Timeline**
:   A positive coordinate axis defined by an origin and a measuring unit;
    continuous (real) or discrete (integer). Accommodates events and
    potentially {{< glossary Child >}} timelines.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimelineGroup**
:   An array of member timelines that share the same graphical start and
    end: every member's 0 coincides with every other member's 0, and every
    member's length with every other member's length. Placing timelines in a
    group asserts {{< glossary Commensurability >}} regardless of their
    units. A position in between converts linearly and exactly (`p` on
    member A is `p · len_B / len_A` on member B) and is written in the target
    member's number type. When only part of a timeline takes part, the member
    is a {{< glossary Child >}} of that timeline at its exact offset; a member
    is never placed partially. No member is an ancestor or a descendant of
    another member of the same group, since a child sits at its offset inside
    its parent. A group answers with the same
    {{< glossary TimeStamp >}} class as a {{< glossary Timeline >}};
    `to_dict()` and `from_dict()` write and read it with every timeline it
    needs.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**TimeStamp**
:   A cross-section through a timeline or group at a given coordinate,
    capturing positions in all connected systems plus values converted by
    all attached {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s. It stores one
    {{< glossary Coordinate >}} per timeline ID, so each entry carries its own
    unit and number type. TimeStamp implements the `Stamp` interface it
    shares with {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}: a typed `axis`,
    `get_coordinate_for()` and
    `get_coordinates_for()` returning {{< glossary IdCoordinate >}}s by
    default, `get_unit()` for unit conversion, `get_conversion_for()` for
    label and structured map values, `present_timelines`, and
    `is_interpolated`. A bare number is an explicit
    `format="float"/"int"/"fraction"` request; there is no ambient float view.
    Which children answer follows the containment rule of
    {{< glossary Child >}}.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**TimeToShare manifest**
:   The file format in which timelines, groups and bundles are exchanged,
    written in canonical YAML, or optionally in pretty JSON or RFC 8785 JSON,
    one shape for all: the version marker `"timetoshare"`, an array of root
    `timelines`, and optionally the manifest's `id`, `name` and `meta`, its
    `groups`, its `measure_maps`, its `resources` (the files beside it, such
    as the MatchClaim table; see {{< glossary Resource >}}), its `@context`,
    `statements` and
    `provenance` (see {{< glossary statement >}}) and its `graphical`
    (display order and styling). A single
    timeline is a manifest of one root, a group a manifest with one group; a
    manifest with an `id` or a `name` is named. Every manifest is an
    alignment bundle, also one holding one timeline or one group, and a
    manifest with neither an `id` nor a `name` is an anonymous bundle. A
    value on a timeline's own axis (`length`, a child's `offset`, region
    bounds, flow-control coordinates) is written bare, in the axis's number
    type.
    {{< glossary Timeline >}}, {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}} and
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} write one with `to_dict()` and read one
    with `from_dict()`, and write and read a manifest file with `to_file()`
    and `from_file()`.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

## U

**Unknown key**
:   A key of a {{< glossary "TimeToShare manifest" >}} that the format does
    not define, written by another application for its own use. The library
    keeps every unknown key on the object read from the JSON object it was
    found in and writes it back in place.

**Unknown length**
:   A timeline length of `None` (`null` in a manifest), stating that the
    length is not known. It is a fact, never inferred from content, and any
    timeline may have it: root, {{< glossary Child >}},
    {{< glossary Locked >}}, group member or {{< glossary Segment >}}.
    Positions on such a timeline are not bounded above, unless its parent
    ends it, as a segment line ends a {{< glossary Segment >}}; an operation
    that needs the end raises {{< glossary UnknownLengthError >}}. Setting a length
    to or from `None` is an ordinary edit; `Timeline.is_length_known` tells
    which case holds, and displays use the {{< glossary Reach >}}.

**UnknownLengthError**
:   The `ValueError` raised by an operation that needs the end of a timeline
    whose length is unknown, before it changes anything. Its message names the
    operation and the timeline; group conversion to or from such a member and
    appending a child at such a parent's end are examples.

## V

**Virtual timeline**
:   The statement that a map was applied to a {{< glossary Timeline >}},
    giving a timeline with an {{< glossary "element id" >}}, a unit, a
    number type and a length of its own and nothing else: no events, no
    children, no flow control. Applied, a {{< glossary FlowMap >}} gives its
    root's played order as a virtual timeline, and positions convert through
    it in both directions (`unfold()`, `fold()`).
    `Timeline.create_virtual_timeline()` states one; a manifest lists them in
    `virtual_timelines`.
    See [How to Encode and Play Flow Control](howto/how01_flow_control.ipynb).

## W

**WarpMap**
:   An interpolation-based coordinate mapping derived from a
    {{< glossary MatchLine >}}; enables non-linear coordinate transfer
    between {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}s. It declares both axes — source
    and target unit *and* number type — and is queried through
    `get_coordinate_at(position)` for one position or
    `get_coordinates_at([...])` for a batch; the object is not callable and
    exposes no raw arrays. `inverse()` returns a WarpMap with both units and
    both number types swapped.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#coordinate-transfer).
